title: High CPU Usage Investigation
question: Investigate and resolve high CPU usage in production. Requirements: 1) CPU at 90%+ constantly, 2) Application slow, 3) No obvious errors in logs, 4) Need root cause. Discuss: using top/htop to identify Java process consuming CPU, using jstack to capture thread dumps, identifying CPU-intensive threads using top -H -p <pid>, correlating thread IDs (convert to hex) with thread dumps, analyzing stack traces for hot methods, looking for tight loops or recursive calls, using profiler (async-profiler, JFR) to identify CPU hotspots, generating flame graphs for visualization, checking for inefficient algorithms, looking for regex compilation in loops, checking database queries without indexes, analyzing GC logs for excessive GC activity causing CPU usage, implementing optimizations (caching, algorithm improvements), and monitoring after fixes.

title: OutOfMemoryError Investigation
question: Debug OutOfMemoryError in production application. Requirements: 1) Application crashes with OOM after 12 hours, 2) Heap dumps available, 3) Find memory leak source, 4) Implement fix. Discuss: analyzing heap dump with MAT, identifying objects consuming most memory using histogram view, finding growth patterns by comparing multiple heap dumps, using dominator tree to find biggest retained objects, checking for static collections, looking for unclosed resources (database connections, file handles), analyzing ThreadLocal usage in thread pools, checking for listener registration without unregistration, using path to GC roots to understand why objects aren't collected, implementing fixes (weak/soft references for caches, proper resource cleanup, removing static collections), configuring -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError for automatic dumps, increasing heap size if genuine memory needs, and implementing monitoring to detect memory growth early.

title: GC Tuning for Low Latency
question: Tune GC for low-latency application. Requirements: 1) Trading application requiring <10ms p99 latency, 2) Current GC pauses 50-100ms, 3) 8GB heap, 4) High throughput. Discuss: switching from Parallel GC to G1 or ZGC, analyzing current GC logs with GCEasy/GCViewer, identifying Full GC causes, tuning G1 with MaxGCPauseMillis target (10ms), setting appropriate heap size (neither too small nor too large), tuning young generation size for object lifetime, implementing object pooling to reduce allocation rate, using concurrent collectors (G1, ZGC, Shenandoah), monitoring GC pauses with JFR, analyzing allocation hotspots with profiler, reducing object creation in hot paths, using primitive types where possible, considering off-heap memory for large data structures, implementing async processing for non-critical paths, and continuous monitoring with Prometheus/Grafana.

title: Container OOM Kill Investigation
question: Debug Kubernetes pod getting OOMKilled. Requirements: 1) Pod crashes with OOMKilled status, 2) Memory limit 2GB, 3) Java application with -Xmx1500m, 4) Intermittent crashes. Discuss: understanding container memory includes heap + metaspace + threads + direct memory + OS, calculating total JVM memory needs (heap + metaspace + code cache + thread stacks + GC overhead), checking direct memory usage (NIO buffers), monitoring actual memory usage with cAdvisor/Prometheus, analyzing native memory with NativeMemoryTracking (-XX:NativeMemoryTracking=detail), using jcmd to print NMT summary, identifying memory-consuming areas (thread stacks with many threads, large metaspace from class loading, direct memory from NIO), setting appropriate memory limits (Kubernetes requests/limits), using -XX:MaxRAMPercentage instead of fixed heap size in containers, implementing graceful degradation, monitoring container metrics, and adjusting resource allocation based on actual usage.
